newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors end meeting on Yeltsin heart op - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Doctors end meeting on Yeltsin heart op - Interfax.

text.p: Doctors have ended their meeting aimed at deciding when and whether to operate on Russian President Boris Yeltsin, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.
The agency gave no clues to the doctors' decisions, saying only that preliminary conclusions and doctors' recommendations would be disclosed "in the coming days".
The fact that the doctors' meeting did not last long might indicate that the specialists decided they needed more information and were not ready to issue a final ruling.

The team which met Yeltsin at the Central Clinical Hospital includes Russian heart specialist Yevgeny Chazov and pioneering U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey. He will advise the Russian team but will not participate in the surgery itself.

The operation is expected to be conducted by Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin. Interfax news agency said Akchurin was likely to fly to Germany soon after the council meeting to consult some experts there.

Yeltsin, 65, has been in the Central Clinical Hospital since September 13 and aides have said doctors are conducting tests and preparing him for a bypass operation which will improve blood supply to the heart.
